about: Repeated-site identity vectors (spec §9.10). Hand-written render-v1; no MPRX, no manifest, no syntax. `keys` is the declared key of each instance of each repeated site, in item order; identity names write a string key quoted and a number bare.

vectors.name: C11-stable-repeated
vectors.about: the same declared keys in the same order: every instance kept, none moved

vectors.name: C12-reorder
vectors.about: the items come in another order: every identity is kept, and each is moved relative to another kept sibling

vectors.name: C13-insert
vectors.about: an item is inserted between two others: they are kept, the new one created

vectors.name: C14-remove-middle
vectors.about: the middle item goes: it is removed, the others kept

vectors.name: C15-remove-first
vectors.about: the first item goes: it is removed, the others kept, though every index changed

vectors.name: C16-duplicate-key
vectors.about: two items of one repeat declare the same key: the render fails closed and no tree exists

vectors.name: C17-invalid-key
vectors.about: an item whose declared key is not a string or a finite number: the render fails closed and no tree exists; the runtime never substitutes the item's position
vectors.notes: NaN and the infinities are also not keys; JSON cannot write them, so there is no vector entry

vectors.name: C18-string-versus-number
vectors.about: the string "1" and the number 1 are different keys, so different identities; removing one keeps the other

vectors.name: C19-zero-normalization
vectors.about: 0 and -0 are the same key: one identity, kept

vectors.name: C20-same-key-different-sites
vectors.about: the key "a" at two repeated sites is two identities, with no collision; removing the second leaves the first

vectors.name: C21-reappearance
vectors.about: [a] → [] → [a]: the identity is the same name in the first and third trees, but its occurrence ended in the second, so the third is created, inheriting nothing

vectors.name: C22-handler-identity
vectors.about: a repeated node's handlers are its identity and the event: stable across a reorder, different for a different key, and different per event
